gate.reason: The course entry, research brief, concept registry, notation ledger, and predecessor agree on one move: evaluate a stationary power-spectrum estimate by keeping ensemble meaning, spectral resolution, variability, windowing, and overlap dependence in one declared measurement contract.

course_contract.goal: Evaluate a stationary power-spectrum estimate through autocorrelation, bias, variance, leakage, overlap, and resolution.
course_contract.opening_verbatim: Random power is an ensemble property, so one finite periodogram must be treated as an estimator rather than a deterministic transform result.
inherits: Peak Estimation and Zero-Padding Limits ended with 50 seeded equal-length white-noise records whose one-bin squared magnitudes had mean 0.021767896, sample standard deviation 0.024899643, and coefficient of variation 1.143870026; padding did not suppress realization-to-realization spread.

Windows, Leakage, and Resolution established periodic-window conventions, main-lobe resolution, coherent response, and ENBW; this lesson retrieves those measurements without rebuilding the window catalog.
DTFT and Frequency Response established the transform pair and sign convention used to connect lag and frequency descriptions.
must_not_reteach: Zero padding as denser sampling of one finite-record DTFT, parabolic peak interpolation, or phase-created false resolution.
The finite-window convolution proof, window-family metric table, coherent-gain derivation, or ENBW derivation.
Time-frequency display, frame-order interpretation, COLA/WOLA, reconstruction, or the subband view; those belong to the STFT lesson.
course_contract.hands_off: The sole forward exercise keeps Welch frames in order only long enough to expose discarded timing information; all STFT terminology, design, and reconstruction remain in stft-spectrograms-and-reconstruction.

single_conceptual_move.statement: Turn a finite squared-magnitude spectrum into an auditable stationary-process estimate: define the ensemble quantity through autocorrelation and PSD, diagnose why one periodogram remains variable, and choose Welch parameters that satisfy resolution and empirical variability together without counting overlap as independent evidence.
single_conceptual_move.success_test: Given a stationary record and a spectral claim, the reader can declare scaling and units, choose segment/window/overlap parameters, predict the resolution cost, measure coefficient of variation over seeded trials, and reject a smooth estimate that hides the requested tones or overstates the independence of overlapped frames.
keeper_facts: For a wide-sense stationary process, autocorrelation r_xx[ell] and PSD S_xx(exp(j omega)) are a DTFT pair under a declared sign, scaling, and unit convention.

Vanishing periodogram bias is insufficient for consistency because the variance at a frequency does not vanish as one record grows; a raw Gaussian-noise ordinate retains coefficient of variation near one.

Averaging K independent periodograms gives idealized coefficient of variation 1/sqrt(K), but overlapped windowed frames are correlated, so the effective reduction must be measured or corrected rather than inferred from frame count.

throughline: Ref the predecessor with the reminder that 50 padded white-noise spectra retained CV about 1.144 at one fixed bin.
Ref the window lesson with the reminder that segment length and window shape already determine main-lobe resolution and ENBW.
State the lesson move as a joint estimator audit: ensemble meaning, bias, variance, resolution, and dependence must all be declared.
retrieval_task: Distinguish N acquired samples from an L-point FFT and state which can change physical resolving evidence.
Name the window measurement that controls separation of close tones and the measurement that calibrates white-noise power.
State the course forward-transform sign and whether the previous lesson's one-bin quantity was amplitude or squared magnitude.
From the predecessor's mean 0.021767896 and standard deviation 0.024899643, recompute the coefficient of variation and interpret what padding failed to change.
opening_and_retrieval.folded_answers: N and the analysis window set the observation aperture; L only changes transform coordinates when data are held fixed. Main-lobe width controls separation and ENBW calibrates white-noise bandwidth. The course uses the unscaled negative-sign forward transform, and the prior statistic was squared magnitude. Its CV is 0.024899643/0.021767896=1.143870026, so realization-to-realization scatter remained of the same order as the mean.
opening_and_retrieval.placement: One closed-book Task with folded answers immediately after the throughline, before random-process vocabulary or formulas.

argument_sections.heading: One record is a realization, not an ensemble
argument_sections.claim: A random process is a probability model for an indexed family of random variables, while one stored record is only one realization; a sample average may estimate an expectation but cannot be silently substituted for it.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Reuse the predecessor's fixed-bin results: 50 records produce a visibly broad set of powers with CV 1.143870026 even though every record has the same N, Hann window, L, scale, and generating law.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Introduce random process, realization, expectation, mean, and the WSS conditions E{x[n]}=mu_x and E{x[n+ell]x*[n]}=r_xx[ell] independent of n. Give a constant random sequence as a structurally different WSS example, a one-sample boundary case, and a deterministic impulse as the near-miss whose time-varying mean/second moment violates WSS.
argument_sections.reversal: A smoother individual plot does not become a better ensemble estimate merely because its grid is dense.
argument_sections.bearing: The target quantity must be defined at the process level before any finite-record estimator can be judged.

argument_sections.heading: Autocorrelation and PSD describe the same stationary power
argument_sections.claim: For a WSS process with an admissible correlation sequence, the lag-domain autocorrelation and frequency-domain PSD are a DTFT pair, so flat white-noise power and concentrated constant-sequence power follow from different correlation structures.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Start with unit-variance zero-mean white noise: r_xx[ell]=delta[ell], so its two-sided PSD is flat at 1 in power per radians/sample under the course convention; contrast x[n]=A, whose r_xx[ell]=E{|A|^2} yields a line at zero frequency.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: State S_xx(exp(j omega))=sum_ell r_xx[ell]exp(-j omega ell) and the inverse with 1/(2 pi). Define PSD as average power per unit frequency and state nonnegativity. Then construct the biased finite-record autocorrelation estimate from lag products, explicitly labeling it hat-r rather than r.
argument_sections.reversal: The finite correlogram may use the same transform algebra as the population pair, but its lag averages remain estimates from one realization.
argument_sections.bearing: Lag products provide a computable route to spectral power while preserving the distinction between population quantity and finite estimate.

argument_sections.heading: A longer raw periodogram does not become stable
argument_sections.claim: The periodogram is a windowed squared-magnitude estimator whose expected smoothing can narrow with record length while its pointwise variance remains of the same order as the squared PSD, so asymptotically small bias does not imply consistency.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Place many seeded periodograms from the same white-noise process on fixed axes, then compare N=256 and N=4096 at one normalized interior frequency: the envelope remains broad even though the longer record's spectral kernel narrows.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Declare a two-sided per-radian periodogram normalization, connect its expectation to smoothing by |W|^2, and define bias, variance, mean-square error, and consistency. For Gaussian white noise, use the exponential-ordinate model to show standard deviation approximately equals the mean and CV approximately equals 1.
argument_sections.reversal: From narrower deterministic leakage one might expect a stable estimate; the raw ordinate instead retains order-one relative scatter.
argument_sections.bearing: A useful refinement must reduce variance rather than merely densify coordinates or lengthen one unaveraged transform.

argument_sections.heading: Welch averaging buys stability with shorter, correlated frames
argument_sections.claim: Welch estimation reduces variance by averaging windowed segment periodograms, but the shorter segment fixes a broader resolution kernel and overlap reuses samples, making adjacent estimates correlated rather than independent evidence.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Average K=16 independent length-M Hann periodograms of seeded white noise: the idealized CV falls from about 1 to 1/sqrt(16)=0.25 while the length-M main lobe, not the full-record length, governs separation. Then overlap adjacent length-M frames by 50 percent and show that empirical CV is larger than an independence claim based only on the raw frame count.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: Define the Welch estimator from segment start indices, window normalization, squared DFTs, and their arithmetic mean. Keep hop notation local to the estimator pipeline, state exact frame count, and distinguish frame count K from effective independent averages. No STFT definition or reconstruction condition appears.
argument_sections.reversal: Overlap creates more estimates without creating the same number of independent observations.
argument_sections.bearing: Welch parameters exchange frequency resolution, variance, and computation under a dependence clause that the report must expose.

argument_sections.heading: A PSD estimate passes only a joint resolution-and-variability test
argument_sections.claim: Estimator quality is claim-dependent: a configuration succeeds only if its segment/window kernel separates the requested components and its empirical coefficient of variation meets the declared threshold over reproducible trials.
argument_sections.concrete_entry: Use the course target of tones 0.04 cycles/sample apart in a 16,384-sample stationary record and require CV below 0.30 over at least 50 seeded trials. Compare a full-record raw periodogram, an extremely short Welch frame, a defensible middle setting, and an extremely long frame.
argument_sections.formal_apparatus: No new theorem. Present a parameter ledger containing record length, segment length, window endpoint convention, hop/overlap, frame count, FFT length, main-lobe width in cycles/sample, one/two-sided units, seed/trial count, measured CV, tone-separation verdict, and overlap-dependence warning.
argument_sections.reversal: The smoothest curve can fail by merging the tones, while the sharpest curve can fail by retaining order-one variability.
argument_sections.bearing: The lesson closes with an auditable estimator choice; the next lesson retains frame order when timing is itself evidence.

global_conventions: Use E{.} only for population expectation and an overbar or hat only for finite sample averages/estimates.
Use ell exclusively for lag in this lesson; use a different local symbol such as m for Welch frame number so the later STFT ledger can own ell as frame index without collision.
Use r_xx[ell] for population autocorrelation and hat-r_xx[ell] for its finite estimate; use S_xx(exp(j omega)) for population PSD and hat-S for estimators.
Declare complex conjugation, forward sign, one/two-sided convention, per-radian or per-Hz units, endpoint doubling, and every 2*pi or f_s factor before comparing values.

terms.first_use: A probability model for random variables indexed by sample number, not a noisy-looking array.
One complete sample sequence drawn from that process.
A process with constant mean and autocorrelation depending only on lag; abbreviate WSS only after this sentence.
Expected product of the process with a conjugated lagged copy under the declared lag orientation.
Average power per unit frequency, Fourier-dual to WSS autocorrelation; state the unit in the same sentence.
Optional name for the DTFT of a finite autocorrelation estimate; use once or omit if it adds no later value.
A scaled squared magnitude of a windowed finite-record DFT used as a PSD estimator.
Expected estimate minus the target quantity.
An estimator whose error vanishes in probability; decreasing bias alone does not meet this contract.
The average of windowed segment periodograms under declared segment starts and normalization.
Reuse of samples by adjacent segments; state the hop and percent reuse together.
The smaller independent-equivalent count implied by correlation among overlapped segment estimates; do not equate it to raw frame count.
Sample standard deviation divided by sample mean across identically configured trials; use only where the mean is positive.
The nondominated settings for which improving measured variability requires accepting a broader segment kernel, or vice versa.

exercise_plan.placement: Exercise 1 is paired in-body with the lag-product worked example in section 2; Exercises 2 through 6 form the mixed closing Exercises section.

exercises.prompt: For x=[1,-1,1,-1], compute the biased autocorrelation estimates at lags 0 through 3 with denominator N=4, mirror the positive lags, and evaluate the finite Fourier sum at omega=0 and pi.
exercises.full_solution: At lag ell, sum the N-ell products and still divide by 4: hat-r[0]=(1+1+1+1)/4=1; hat-r[1]=(-1-1-1)/4=-3/4; hat-r[2]=(1+1)/4=1/2; hat-r[3]=(-1)/4=-1/4. For this real record hat-r[-ell]=hat-r[ell]. Thus hat-S(0)=1+2(-3/4+1/2-1/4)=0, while hat-S(pi)=1+2[(-3/4)(-1)+(1/2)(1)+(-1/4)(-1)]=4. The alternating record concentrates the finite estimated power at omega=pi under this convention; the calculation is an estimate from one record, not a population PSD proof.

exercises.prompt: Classify zero-mean white noise, a deterministic impulse sequence, a constant random sequence x[n]=A, and a length-N record queried at |ell|>=N. For each, state whether a WSS population autocorrelation/PSD and a finite lag estimate are defined and what the boundary teaches.
exercises.full_solution: Zero-mean white noise is WSS with r[ell]=sigma^2 delta[ell] and a flat two-sided PSD sigma^2. A deterministic impulse at a fixed time is not WSS: its mean/second moment depends on absolute n, although one may compute a finite deterministic correlation sequence without calling it the population PSD of a stationary process. For x[n]=A for every n, with finite E{|A|^2}, the process is WSS and r[ell]=E{|A|^2}; its periodic-frequency PSD is 2*pi*E{|A|^2} times the line train at omega=0 modulo 2*pi, not a flat spectrum. At |ell|>=N no sample pairs overlap; the biased finite convention may return zero by zero extension, while the unbiased denominator N-|ell| reaches zero at |ell|=N and is undefined. In neither case does a missing product supply evidence about the population lag.

exercises.prompt: Refute: 'The periodogram is consistent because its expected value approaches the PSD as N grows.' Separate bias, variance, and mean-square error, and give the white-noise counterexample.
exercises.full_solution: Consistency requires the estimation error to vanish, not only its expectation. Mean-square error decomposes as variance plus squared bias. Window-kernel smoothing can make periodogram bias shrink at an interior continuity point as N grows, but for Gaussian white noise a normalized interior periodogram ordinate is approximately exponential: its mean is S, its variance is S^2, and its coefficient of variation is 1. Hence bias can approach zero while variance and MSE remain nonzero. The failed inference replaces 'asymptotically unbiased' with 'consistent'; averaging or smoothing across independent evidence is the missing operation.

exercises.prompt: Using the declared seeded generator, reproduce a raw-periodogram versus K=16 independent-periodogram average at one interior white-noise frequency over 50 trials. Report both CVs and 95-percent bootstrap confidence intervals, and state what agreement with the ideal 1 and 1/sqrt(16) predictions means.
exercises.full_solution: Freeze the generator, N or segment M, periodic Hann coefficients, FFT length, two-sided per-radian normalization, interior bin, and 50 outer trials. In each outer trial record one raw ordinate P_1 and the mean P_bar=(1/16)sum_{k=1}^{16}P_k from independent records. Compute sample CV=s/mean for each 50-value vector. Resample each vector with replacement at least 10,000 times using a second fixed seed and take the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of bootstrap CV. The population model predicts CV(P_1)=1 and CV(P_bar)=1/4 when the ordinates are independent exponentials; finite-trial estimates need not equal those numbers exactly, but their intervals should contain or lie near them under the frozen tolerance. A result far outside prompts checks of scaling, independence, bin endpoints, or generator variance before any theory claim.

exercises.prompt: For a stationary 16,384-sample record with tones 0.04 cycles/sample apart in seeded white noise, choose between one full-record periodogram and Welch estimates. Predeclare segment length, periodic window, overlap, FFT length, predicted resolution, and a 50-trial CV check; explain which cues decide.
exercises.full_solution: The first cue is that two simultaneous requirements differ: separation depends on the segment window's main lobe, while stability depends on averaging. One defensible starting design is periodic Hann M=512, hop 256, and FFT length at least 512. The Hann null-to-null width is approximately 4/M=0.0078125 cycles/sample, well below the 0.04 separation; padding may make the display denser but does not change that width. The frame count is floor((16384-512)/256)+1=63, but 50-percent overlap makes adjacent estimates correlated, so 1/sqrt(63) is not accepted as the CV claim. Run the frozen 50 trials and require measured CV below 0.30 while the declared two-tone separation rule passes. A full-record periodogram easily separates the tones but retains CV near one; very short segments may lower CV yet merge the tones. The exact passing preset is empirical, and the ledger must report window ENBW/scaling retrieved from the window lesson rather than compare raw uncalibrated powers.

exercises.prompt: In a stationary-noise record, let the second of two tones begin halfway through. Compute the same windowed segment periodograms used by Welch, first retaining their time order and then averaging them. Locate the onset as tightly as the declared frame/hop permits and identify exactly what the average discards.
exercises.full_solution: For each segment, track its start index and the power in the second tone's frequency neighborhood. Before onset those ordered values stay at the noise floor; frames whose support straddles the onset rise gradually; after onset they remain elevated. The earliest defensible onset interval is bounded by the first elevated frame's support, and its reporting granularity is limited jointly by frame duration and hop, not FFT padding. Averaging the same segment periodograms produces one frequency curve and removes the association between spectral power and frame position, so it cannot say when the tone began. Keeping the ordered spectra creates the object developed in <Ref lesson="stft-spectrograms-and-reconstruction">STFT, Spectrograms, and Reconstruction</Ref>; this is the sole forward Ref and no reconstruction claim is made here.
